item.title: Russia will launch a routine ISS supply mission tomorrow—apparently, it's a big secret
item.description: It was the most simple of questions. On Monday afternoon, during a NASA news conference about the International Space Station, Space News reporter Jeff Foust asked about an upcoming launch of a Russian spacecraft. "It's my understanding there's another cargo mission going to the ISS this week, a Russian Progress," Foust said. "Can you confirm that, and give the date and time that will launch?" This Progress MS-36 cargo launch, mind you, is presently scheduled for fewer than 16 hours from now, at 10:13 UTC (05:13 am ET) on Tuesday. It is going to a space station co-operated by the US space agency. But no, NASA would not provide this basic information about the upcoming Progress launch. Read full article Comments

item.title: Surveillance pricing uses our personal data to make us pay more
item.description: “It costs what it costs” is a mindset I’ve found useful when encountering a sizable, but highly necessary or desired, expense. The sentiment encourages me to accept the price because that’s the accepted value of the gadget, app, or service that I really need or want. But with surveillance pricing, that comfort is no longer a given. I could end up paying more for my TV because of where I am or more for a software subscription because of my age. Surveillance pricing leverages data collected from our web history , smart devices , and apps with the goal of getting us to pay more. That obfuscates the value of products, challenges smart shopping and budgets, and makes it harder for people to get the products and services at a fair price. Read full article Comments

item.title: HBO Max is offering one of the best Black Friday deals we’ve seen this year
item.description: If you’ve been meaning to catch up on Lanterns or the latest season of The Gilded Age , Thanksgiving weekend is the perfect time to do so. And thanks to HBO Max’s new Black Friday deal, new and returning subscribers can now watch both shows for less. The streaming service is currently offering a 50 percent discount for Black Friday , bringing the price of its Basic With Ads plan down to $5.49 per month (about $6 off) for one year. The promotion runs through November 30th, and you can subscribe either via HBO Max or Amazon . HBO Max Where to Buy: $10.49 $5.49 at Amazon (monthly, with ads) $10.99 $5.49 at HBO Max (monthly, with ads) HBO Max has plenty of great movies and shows to keep you entertained well into the new year, no matter which plan you choose. You’ll find a wide selection of TV shows, including Heated Rivalry , Dune: Prophecy , The White Lotus , Euphoria , and Knight of the Seven Kingdoms , alongside longtime favorites like Game of Thrones and The Big Bang Theory . There’s more on the way, too, including HBO’s highly anticipated Harry Potter series, which premieres on Christmas . There’s plenty to watch beyond TV, too. HBO Max’s extensive movie catalog currently includes films like Sinners , One Battle After Another , Marty Supreme , Backrooms , and Wuthering Heights . And if you’re a sports fan, both the Standard and Premium plans also include access to select live events from MLB, U.S. Soccer, the NCAA, and more. What you get ultimately depends on the subscription tier you choose. HBO Max’s Basic with Ads plan lets you stream on two devices at once but doesn’t include live sports. The ad-free Standard plan ($18.49 a month), meanwhile, adds live sports and up to 30 offline downloads. The Premium plan ($22.99 a month) adds a few more perks, including 4K streaming and Dolby Atmos with select titles, up to 100 downloads, and the ability to stream movies and shows on four devices simultaneously. That said, HBO currently isn’t offering discounts on either the Standard or Premium plans… at least not yet.

item.title: Amazon fights Delivery Protection Act by putting stickers on its packages

This weekend, some Amazon shoppers reported getting a delivery from Amazon with a sticker on it that reads: “NYC Council could add up to $5 per order. Act now to protect low prices.” The sticker reportedly includes a QR code that leads to a link for contacting NYC Councilmembers. The sticker encourages the package’s recipient to “Scan to tell your council member: no increases for New Yorkers.” Amazon is looking to stoke opposition to Introduction 0518-2026 ( 518 ), also known as the Delivery Protection Act. The proposed law would require Amazon and other companies with last-mile delivery facilities in the city, such as FedEx, to directly employ third-party contractors Amazon uses for making deliveries. item.title: Reports: Russia may launch nuclear weapon into orbit as soon as next month
item.description: Western intelligence officials worry that Russia could launch a nuclear-armed satellite into orbit before the end of the year, suggesting the country's development of a satellite-killing weapon of mass destruction is more advanced than previously thought, German media reported Monday. The orbiting nuclear weapon would threaten thousands of satellites in low-Earth orbit, including military and commercial communications networks like Starshield and Starlink. A nuclear-armed satellite would also put at risk Western military surveillance satellites and human spaceflight platforms like the International Space Station. A nuclear detonation in orbit would be indiscriminate, also knocking out Russia's own spacecraft and Chinese satellites. US lawmakers briefed on government intelligence first disclosed Russia's ambition to deploy a space-based nuclear weapon in early 2024 . At the time, US officials said Russia had launched a test satellite in 2022 to test the effects of radiation on space hardware and pave the way for a future nuclear-armed craft, but that Russia had not yet sent a nuclear weapon into orbit. Read full article Comments

item.title: Marvel crams every superhero ever into Avengers: Doomsday final trailer
item.description: Rumors have been swirling for days that we would be getting a final trailer for Avengers: Doomsday , the penultimate film in the Marvel Cinematic Universe’s Phase Six, heralding the end of the so-called “Multiverse Saga.” The rumors were true: Marvel just released the trailer, featuring pretty much every superhero ever represented in the MCU. And it looks like the Avengers will face consequences for messing with the timeline to reverse the blip in Endgame . As previously reported , the film takes place 14 months after the events of Thunderbolts* . Per the official logline: “Beloved heroes from three distinct universes will be set on a deadly collision course and face an existential threat unlike anything they’ve ever encountered.” Those universes are Earth-616 (the Avengers, Wakandans, and New Avengers), Earth-828 (Fantastic Four), and the “original” X-Men. Cast-wise, we have Avengers favorites Thor (Chris Hemsworth), the new Captain America (Anthony Mackie), Bucky Barnes (Sebastian Stan), Ant-Man (Paul Rudd), Falcon (Danny Ramirez), and Loki (Tom Hiddleston). Then there’s the Wakandan contingent: Shuri as the new Black Panther (Letitia Wright), M’Baku (Winston Duke), and Namor (Tenoch Huerta Mejia), as well as Alex Livinalli as Namor’s ally, Attuma. And, of course, Robert Downey Jr. as Doctor Doom. Read full article Comments

item.title: F1 in Las Vegas: You've never seen an F1 race like this before
item.description: Las Vegas welcomed Formula 1 to its streets this past weekend. And for the first time since the event’s inception in 2023 , the Grand Prix delivered on a long-promised spectacle. The racing was closer to an IndyCar oval race than anything F1 fans will have seen since slipstreaming was the order of the day at places like Monza and Hockenheim, back when humans were still landing on the Moon and downforce had yet to fundamentally change racing. The Vegas street circuit—the one that looks like an upside-down pig—is an extreme outlier on the calendar. It has plenty of long straights, so this year’s cars still suffer from energy starvation throughout the lap, as the inadequate size of their lithium-ion hybrid batteries means they become depleted very quickly , leaving the cars on just over half power with their V6 engines operating without the benefit of the hybrid’s electric motor. But the 17 turns are mostly all low speed, so there’s no risk of seeing the cars driving demoralizingly slowly through corners that are supposed to test one’s mettle . Read full article Comments

While it doesn't have a traditional GPU, the Asus ProArt P16 , with up to 128GB of memory, can also be your primary gaming and productivity machine, but this unified experience comes at a high price. If you want to run a small army of agents on your laptop, you're looking at $7,000 for the top-end ProArt P16, and despite being more approachable on Windows, local AI still requires a lot of trial and error. The PC stuff Before we dive into the AI agents, let's talk about the ProArt P16 as a laptop. Nvidia's pitch is that the RTX Spark can be your one true machine for AI, productivity, and gaming. item.title: GLP-1 drugs could have a surprisingly large environmental payoff
item.description: GLP-1 weight-loss medicines such as Ozempic and Wegovy could affect much more than the waistlines of the people who take them. If widely used, our new research suggests these appetite-suppressing medicines could transform the global food system and free up vast areas of agricultural land. The global food system is ultimately driven by demand. If people eat less, producers respond, affecting production, prices, trade, and how much land is needed. We used a powerful computer simulation to explore scenarios ranging from GLP-1 use concentrated in high-income countries to widespread global access. With widespread use of these medicines among adults living with obesity, we estimate that reduced calorie intake could prevent up to 6.6 million deaths each year by 2050, while freeing up as much as 32 million hectares of agricultural land—an area slightly larger than Italy—for other uses. Read full article Comments

item.title: Review: Godzilla Minus Zero joins the ranks of truly stellar sequels
item.description: It's a rare thing for a film sequel to match or even surpass its predecessor; The Godfather Part II and Terminator 2: Judgment Day are the best-known examples. Go ahead and add Godzilla Minus Zero to that list. Director Takashi Yamazaki's sequel to his critically acclaimed Godzilla Minus One (2023) is everything one could want in a Godzilla movie: human pathos, great special effects, and, ultimately, two giant kaiju duking it out over who gets to destroy Japan (and eventually the world) the most. (Spoilers for the first film below. Spoilers for Minus Zero but no major reveals until after the gallery. We'll give you a heads-up when we get there.) As I wrote previously , Yamazaki wanted to return to Godzilla’s filmic roots with Minus One , setting the events in postwar Japan and tapping into the monster’s symbolic representation of the Japanese perspective on the 1940s nuclear holocaust—while also incorporating all-too-human themes of guilt and redemption. That first film focused on kamikaze pilot Kōichi Shikishima (Ryunosuke Kamiki), who struggled with survivor’s guilt after he failed to take action when Godzilla attacked the Japanese base on Odo Island in 1945. Read full article Comments

item.title: “Race realism” isn’t realistic—and it isn’t good science
item.description: At this year’s World Economic Forum meeting in Davos, US President Donald Trump stated that people from Somalia have low IQs. “I always say these are low-IQ people,” he said in his speech. His son, Donald Trump Jr, made a similar statement about Haitian people in 2024 (Trump’s government has since ended the protected status of both Somali and Haitian migrants in the US). These statements and their consequences are symptoms of a growing trend in Western politics: the re-emergence of racial views of human nature that have been largely in hiding for the past 70 years. Narratives about the innate intellectual inferiority of black or brown people compared with white people—which can still be found in academic journals today—are fuelling far-right propaganda in some of the world’s largest democracies. Such claims underpin misinformation strategies on social media and bolster political movements. These narratives are sometimes euphemistically referred to as “ race science ” or more recently “race realism.” But, as we argue, they are not actually scientific. One member of this community, Nathan Cofnas , recently attracted public attention by accusing the late Jason Arday of plagiarism. Read full article Comments

item.title: Trump FCC declares California isn't allowed to enforce phone service rules

item.title: Researcher plants 2m canaries into the AI supply chain. A privacy disaster surfaced.
item.description: Researchers planted 2 million digital tripwires in requests sent through a sprawling network of AI services to find out what happened to sensitive information entrusted to them. What they discovered was an ecosystem that leaked highly sensitive data like a sieve. The exposure was found through an ingenious experiment designed to test if sensitive information can leak through the vast chain of widely used AI services and how that information is exploited when it does. Many of today’s AI apps use services such as OpenRouter or Vercel that act as brokers. These “AI routers,” sometimes also known as “AI gateways,” receive large numbers of prompts sent from AI app end users and route them to an available inference engine based on criteria such as the one charging the lowest price or being best suited for the given task. Instead of using Anthropic, OpenAI, or another big provider, the developer hires an AI router to find the most suitable model. Update, Nov 21: Posts on both Hacker News and X report that OpenRouter has sent customers an email notifying them that some of their prompts may have been read. OpenRouter cited the research and said that it received a report that the potential exposure involved prompts sent to MiniMax, a China-based model provider. OpenRouter said the researchers' planted URLs were accessed whether the prompts were sent to MiniMax directly or through three other resellers: AtlasCloud, Novita, and StreamLake. OpenRouter has removed a "Zero Data Retention" label from MiniMax-model endpoints. Hat tip: Sulat.com . Read full article Comments

item.title: Watching as a giant star swallowed its neighbor and exploded
item.description: In the Andromeda Galaxy, a giant star about seven times as massive as the Sun spent nearly a decade slowly swallowing its much smaller companion. The process, known as common envelope evolution, was proposed in the 1970s to explain how some of the tightest pairs of stars in the Universe form, but no one had ever caught it in the act. In a new Nature study, astronomers led by Viraj Karambelkar, an astrophysicist at Columbia University, finally witnessed the entire spectacle from the decades before it began to the eruption that ended it in late 2025. “It lasts for a few years, maybe a few decades,” Karambelkar said. “Stars evolve on time scales of millions of years. So, it's really like a blip on the entire cosmic time scale.” Shared envelopes Some pairs of stars orbit so close to each other that they could not have formed at that distance, so their orbits must have shrunk. Common envelope evolution is the leading explanation for that shrinkage. When one star in a binary grows old, it expands into a giant, and its outer layers can engulf its companion. The two then share a single, loosely bound envelope of gas. As the engulfed star drags through it, it loses orbital energy to friction and spirals inward. Depending on how much of the envelope gets lost, the pair either ends up in a much tighter orbit or merges. Read full article Comments

item.title: NASA’s new Moon plan is taking shape, but some big questions remain
item.description: SpaceX's successful recovery of its Starship rocket last weekend cleared a major hurdle on NASA's path to the Moon, opening up possibilities for higher launch rates and an all-important, long-delayed orbital refueling demo next year. For SpaceX's purposes, Saturday's mid-air rocket catch will help engineers learn how to rapidly reuse Starships. That should expedite SpaceX's deployment of its newest generation of Starlink Internet satellites. NASA, meanwhile, believes a higher launch cadence will lead to faster learning as SpaceX develops a deep space version of Starship to ferry astronaut crews to the surface of the Moon. Early next year, SpaceX plans to bring online a second Starship launch site at Kennedy Space Center, Florida. A second Starship factory is also under construction at Kennedy, joining SpaceX's existing SpaceX production line at Starbase, Texas. With two launch sites, SpaceX will have the pieces in place to take the next leap with Starship. Read full article Comments
